thread.title: Rep. Rob Menendez addresses ICE funding and community events in latest tweets

author: r. h. wasson
title: Rep. Rob Menendez addresses ICE funding and community events in latest tweets
text:
Rep. Rob Menendez, U.S. Congressman representing New Jersey’s 8th district since 2023, posted a series of tweets on June 9, 2026, addressing immigration enforcement, advocacy for detainees, and community engagement.
In a tweet from the morning of June 9, Menendez criticized recent legislative efforts to increase funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), stating, “More than 6,200 children have been taken by ICE since Trump took office. The parents of at least 27,000 children have been ripped from their families. And this week, House Republicans want to hand ICE $70B more to carry out this cruel assault on our communities.” He posted this statement amid ongoing national debates over border security and immigration policy.
Later that day, Menendez highlighted his appearance on a media platform to discuss the conditions faced by detainees at Delaney Hall. He wrote, “I recently joined @MeidasTouch to share the stories of the individuals held at Delaney Hall. We will never stop fighting to uplift them and working toward a future where facilities like Delaney Hall no longer exist. Watch the full episode below https://t.co/JIUSuE6Ioa” This message reflects Menendez’s ongoing advocacy for detainee rights and reform of detention practices.
On the same afternoon, Menendez also shared his participation in a local event in Hoboken: “Annual Southwest Fest in @CityofHoboken Great day with @HobokenEmily, Councilman Ramos, and Councilman Quintero connecting with so many friends and neighbors. Always look forward to this annual event and thank you to all the local businesses, volunteers, and groups who make https://t.co/OHOIyjk8Jp”
Rob Menendez succeeded Albio Sires as representative for New Jersey’s 8th district in 2023. Born in Hudson County in 1985 and currently residing in Jersey City, he holds degrees from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (BA) and Rutgers University-Newark (JD). His public statements reflect both his legislative priorities regarding immigration enforcement and his engagement with local communities.
